provenance: Signs and actions follow WHO Emergency Triage Assessment and Treatment (ETAT), the IMNCI general danger signs, and the WHO young-infant (possible serious bacterial infection) assessment. Thresholds and wording are an engineering seed and are NOT a ratified national protocol; they require MoHCC and paediatric specialist sign-off before they drive care. See docs/clinical-governance/edliz-engineering-seed-policy.md.

rules.name: Obstructed or threatened airway
rules.message: Airway or breathing emergency — manage the airway now.
rules.explanation: Obstructed breathing, stridor at rest or central cyanosis is an ETAT emergency sign requiring immediate airway management before any further assessment.
rules.requiredAction: Open and clear the airway, give oxygen, and call for senior help. Do not continue the assessment first.
rules.monitoringInstruction: Continuous observation with pulse oximetry until the airway is secure.
sourceRefs: WHO ETAT — emergency signs (airway and breathing)

testCases.name: all signs absent does not fire
nothing assessed does not fire but is incomplete

rules.name: Severe respiratory distress
rules.message: Severe respiratory distress — give oxygen and treat as severe pneumonia until proven otherwise.
rules.explanation: Oxygen saturation below 90%, severe chest indrawing or grunting indicates severe respiratory distress in a child.
rules.requiredAction: Give oxygen, position the child, start treatment for severe pneumonia, and arrange urgent referral if the facility cannot provide oxygen and monitoring.
rules.monitoringInstruction: Reassess breathing and saturation every 15 minutes until stable.
sourceRefs: WHO IMNCI — severe pneumonia or very severe disease

testCases.name: saturation 96 with no other sign does not fire

rules.name: Circulatory failure
rules.message: Signs of shock — give fluids according to protocol now.
rules.explanation: Cold hands with capillary refill longer than three seconds and a weak fast pulse together indicate circulatory failure. Blood pressure falls late in children, so waiting for hypotension loses time.
rules.requiredAction: Give oxygen, obtain vascular access and give a fluid bolus per protocol, check glucose, and call for senior help.
rules.monitoringInstruction: Reassess perfusion and conscious level after each bolus.

testCases.name: cold hands alone does not fire

rules.name: Coma or active convulsion
rules.message: Coma or convulsion — protect the airway, check glucose, and treat the convulsion.
rules.explanation: A child responding only to pain or not at all, or convulsing now, is an ETAT emergency.
rules.requiredAction: Position the airway, give oxygen, check blood glucose immediately and treat hypoglycaemia, give an anticonvulsant if still fitting.
rules.monitoringInstruction: Continuous observation of airway, breathing and conscious level.
sourceRefs: WHO ETAT — emergency signs (coma and convulsions)

testCases.name: alert and not convulsing does not fire

rules.name: Severe dehydration in a child with diarrhoea
rules.message: Diarrhoea with signs of severe dehydration — start rehydration now.
rules.explanation: Diarrhoea together with sunken eyes, a slow skin pinch or altered conscious level indicates severe dehydration.
rules.requiredAction: Start intravenous or intraosseous rehydration per protocol; if not possible, start nasogastric rehydration and arrange urgent referral.
rules.monitoringInstruction: Reassess hydration and conscious level hourly during rehydration.

testCases.name: diarrhoea with slow skin pinch fires

rules.name: IMNCI general danger signs
rules.message: General danger sign present — this child needs urgent referral after pre-referral treatment.
rules.explanation: Any general danger sign in a child aged two months to five years means very severe disease, whatever the presenting complaint.
rules.requiredAction: Give the first dose of appropriate pre-referral treatment, keep the child warm, treat hypoglycaemia, and refer urgently.
rules.monitoringInstruction: Do not delay referral to complete the rest of the assessment.
sourceRefs: WHO IMNCI — assess and classify the sick child aged 2 months to 5 years

testCases.name: all four absent does not fire

rules.name: Possible serious bacterial infection in a young infant
rules.message: Possible serious bacterial infection in an infant under two months — start antibiotics and refer urgently.
rules.explanation: In the first two months of life the signs of severe infection are few and non-specific, and deterioration is rapid. Any one of poor feeding, convulsions, movement only on stimulation, fever, hypothermia, fast breathing or severe chest indrawing is treated as possible serious bacterial infection.
rules.requiredAction: Give the first dose of injectable antibiotics, keep the infant warm and feeding, treat hypoglycaemia, and refer urgently with the mother.
rules.monitoringInstruction: Keep warm and monitor breathing and feeding continuously until transfer.
sourceRefs: WHO IMNCI — young infant age up to 2 months
WHO — management of possible serious bacterial infection in young infants

testCases.name: well infant with everything assessed does not fire

rules.name: Hypoglycaemia
rules.message: Blood glucose below 2.5 mmol/L — treat hypoglycaemia immediately.
rules.explanation: Hypoglycaemia is common in sick and malnourished children and causes avoidable brain injury; it is corrected before anything else.
rules.requiredAction: Give glucose per protocol (intravenous dextrose, or expressed breast milk or sugar water by nasogastric tube if access is not available), then recheck.
rules.monitoringInstruction: Recheck blood glucose after 30 minutes and continue feeding.

rules.name: Severe acute malnutrition with a danger sign
rules.message: Severe acute malnutrition with complications — admit for inpatient stabilisation.
rules.explanation: A child with severe acute malnutrition who fails the appetite test or has a danger sign cannot be managed as an outpatient.
rules.requiredAction: Admit for stabilisation: treat hypoglycaemia and hypothermia, start cautious feeding and antibiotics per protocol. Do not give a standard fluid bolus.
rules.monitoringInstruction: Monitor glucose, temperature and feeding closely during the stabilisation phase.
sourceRefs: WHO guideline on the prevention and management of wasting and nutritional oedema (2023)

testCases.name: oedema with failed appetite test fires
low MUAC with passed appetite and no danger sign does not fire
